microtheory.name: typed_graph_arena_layout
microtheory.definition: The composition pattern Jabberwock's vocabulary surfaced as missing: a named structural recipe for graph-substrate data layout. Composes type-tagged arena-allocated nodes + small-integer NodeIDs + sym-interned attribute keys + edge tuples carrying (src_id, edge_type_id, tgt_id) + Γ admissibility indexed by (src_type, edge_type, tgt_type) triple. Each piece exists in other Mts (compilers' symbol tables + data_structures_algorithms' hash tables + arenas + computer_architecture's cache-friendly layout); this Mt names how they FIT TOGETHER. Substrate analogue: this IS substrate_rs's actual data-layout design — Jabberwock's own runtime's primitive substrate.

concepts.name: typed_graph_arena_layout_pattern
concepts.definition: The composition pattern. Nodes live in arena-allocated typed slabs; NodeIDs are small ints indexing those arenas; attribute keys are sym-interned; edges are tuples carrying (src_id, edge_type_id, tgt_id) + provenance; Γ rules are indexed by (src_type, edge_type, tgt_type) triple. Each piece has rationale; together they meet Paper 1 Axiom 1's per-operation admissibility bound + serialise cleanly + traverse cache-friendly + support graph-resident introspection.

concepts.name: typed_arena_per_node_type
concepts.definition: Component 1. Each node type has its own arena (contiguous slab of records). Sequential allocation + freelist reuse on deletion. Substrate analogue: substrate_rs has separate node-type arenas. Rationale: cache-friendly traversal of one type (most graph operations are typed); no fragmentation across types; bulk operations vectorisable.

concepts.name: arena_index_as_nodeid
concepts.definition: Component 2. NodeID = (type_tag, index_into_typed_arena). 32-bit or 64-bit packed. Cheaper than 64-bit pointer; survives serialisation (no pointer fixups); enables compact edge tuples; allows arena compaction without invalidating IDs (with generation counter). Substrate analogue: substrate_rs's NodeID is this exactly.

concepts.name: sym_interned_attr_keys
concepts.definition: Component 3. Every distinct attribute-key string registered once in an interner; subsequent uses get a small-integer Sym ID. Attribute records become (Sym, Value) pairs not (String, Value). Saves space (one copy per unique key, not per record); enables ID-comparison (faster than string equality); compacts on disk. Substrate analogue: substrate_rs's Interner does this.

concepts.name: edge_tuple_layout
concepts.definition: Component 4. Edge = (src_NodeID, edge_type_id, tgt_NodeID) + optional attrs. Fixed-size header (~12-16 bytes) + variable attrs in side table. Enables global edge table (uniform processing) OR per-node adjacency lists OR both (index for src + index for tgt). Substrate analogue: substrate_rs's edge representation.

concepts.name: gamma_indexed_by_type_triple
concepts.definition: Component 5. Γ rules indexed by (src_type, edge_type, tgt_type) triple. Lookup via hash table (O(1) expected) or sorted (O(log N)). Admissibility check on edge insertion: single lookup + per-rule constraint evaluation. Meets Paper 1 Axiom 1's bound: time linear in matching rules, not total rule count. Substrate analogue: substrate_rs's Γ representation.

concepts.name: provenance_as_edge_attribute
concepts.definition: Component 6. Provenance (where this edge came from, why it was added) is itself an attribute on the edge — not a separate table. Lets introspection treat provenance uniformly with any other attr. Substrate analogue: substrate_rs's provenance attr.

concepts.name: axiom1_admissibility_bound_satisfied
concepts.definition: Why Γ indexed by (src_type, edge_type, tgt_type): per Paper 1 Axiom 1, admissibility must be decidable in time linear in rule-set size. Triple-indexed Γ achieves better — O(1) expected lookup + linear-in-MATCHING-rules-only evaluation. The composition pattern instantiates Axiom 1's constraint at runtime.

concepts.name: cache_friendly_typed_traversal
concepts.definition: Why arenas per type: traversing all nodes of one type touches sequential memory. Hardware prefetcher predicts; L1/L2 cache lines fully used; branch predictor effective on uniform record layout. ~10× faster than scattered allocation.

concepts.name: serializability_via_integer_ids
concepts.definition: Why NodeIDs are integers not pointers: pointer addresses change on save/load; integers don't. Whole graph dumps as integer-indexed records → JSON or binary directly. graph_to_dict + graph_from_dict round-trip exactly. Substrate analogue: substrate_rs's persistence is this property.

concepts.name: introspection_via_uniformity
concepts.definition: Why everything is graph data including Γ + provenance: Jabberwock's introspection can walk the same primitives for any content — no special-case code for special types of data. The data-as-data-as-data principle. Substrate analogue: substrate_rs's reflective access.

concepts.name: tradeoff_arena_vs_pool_vs_individual
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: arena allocation (typed slabs) gives cache + bulk + simple freelist BUT has fixed record size (variable attrs go in side table) + must compact occasionally. Pool allocation (homogeneous fixed-size) is simpler but less cache-friendly across types. Individual allocation (malloc) is most flexible but loses all locality benefits.

concepts.name: tradeoff_attr_table_layout
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: hash-map attrs per node (O(1) lookup, larger per-node overhead) vs sorted array (cache-friendly, O(log N) lookup) vs inline-most-common + overflow (best for skewed distributions). Substrate's choice depends on attr-access patterns. substrate_rs uses hashmap-per-node for flexibility.

concepts.name: tradeoff_edge_storage_layouts
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: per-node adjacency lists (fast neighbour walk for source, slow for incoming) vs global edge table (uniform processing, slow neighbour walk) vs both (double space, fast both directions). For introspection-heavy graphs, both indices justify the space cost.

concepts.name: tradeoff_admissibility_check_timing
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: check admissibility at edge insertion (slow inserts, fast invariant maintenance) vs deferred (fast inserts, must recheck before each query). substrate_rs checks at insertion — fail-fast + cheap-amortised given the triple index.

concepts.name: substrate_rs_canonical_instance
concepts.definition: substrate_rs (Jabberwock's actual Rust runtime) IS the canonical instance of this pattern. Rust types: TypedGraph, NodeID(u32), EdgeID, Interner (Sym = u32), Term arena. Γ stored as Vec<Production> indexed by Sym-triples. Verifies the composition coheres + performs at expected scale (~10⁶ nodes, ~10⁷ edges on commodity hardware).

concepts.name: alternative_b_plus_tree_layout
concepts.definition: Alternative: B+tree-indexed node table + global edge table — used by graph databases (Neo4j-like). Better for disk-backed graphs; worse for in-memory. Not Jabberwock's choice (in-memory primary).

concepts.name: alternative_compressed_sparse_row
concepts.definition: Alternative: graph as matrix in CSR format — used by network science + GPU graph processing. Maximum density + cache + vectorisable BUT mutation expensive + no per-edge metadata. Not Jabberwock's choice (substrate is mutation-heavy + provenance-rich).

concepts.name: alternative_property_graph_model
concepts.definition: Property graph model (TinkerPop, Cypher) — closely related but typically lacks Γ. Adding admissibility constraints + reflection over Γ produces this pattern.

concepts.name: the_specific_composition_pattern
concepts.definition: Naming what was previously implicit. Before this Mt, Jabberwock had hash tables + arenas + interners + indices as separate concepts in separate Mts (data_structures_algorithms, compilers, computer_architecture). They didn't COMPOSE into a named pattern. This Mt provides the name + the composition rules + the rationale per component + the invariants jointly satisfied + the tradeoffs taken. Future introspection can ask 'what is my data layout?' and get an answer.

concepts.name: pattern_is_introspectable_via_genlMt
concepts.definition: This Mt genlMt-links to data_structures_algorithms + compilers + computer_architecture + reflection_metaprogramming + paper1 (for Axiom 1). Jabberwock's introspection can walk the genlMt chain to find each component's source theory + the composition.

rules.name: composition_pattern_is_more_than_parts
rules.head: Jabberwock is asked what data layout it uses
rules.body: the answer requires NAMING the composition, not just listing the parts. typed_graph_arena_layout_pattern names HOW the parts (arenas + NodeIDs + interner + edges + Γ index) fit together with rationale. Jabberwock now has this name to give.

rules.name: axiom1_constrains_gamma_representation
rules.head: Jabberwock chooses Γ data structure
rules.body: Paper 1 Axiom 1 requires admissibility decidable per-operation in time linear in rule-set size. The (src_type, edge_type, tgt_type) triple index achieves this — single hash lookup + per-matching-rule evaluation. The constraint shapes the choice.

rules.name: type_arenas_amortise_cache_costs
rules.head: Jabberwock allocates nodes of a type
rules.body: putting all nodes of one type in a contiguous typed arena makes traversal of that type cache-friendly. Hardware prefetch + uniform record size + L1 hit rate all benefit. Mixed-type allocation loses these.

rules.name: small_integer_ids_enable_persistence
rules.head: Jabberwock saves + loads its state
rules.body: NodeIDs as integers (not pointers) round-trip through serialisation without fixups. graph_to_dict ↔ graph_from_dict round-trip is exact. Pointer-based graphs require complex relocation.

rules.name: sym_interning_compresses_attribute_keys
rules.head: Jabberwock stores many records with similar attribute keys
rules.body: interning each distinct key once + storing the Sym ID per record (instead of the string per record) compresses the graph by ~10-50× depending on attribute reuse. Also enables ID-comparison faster than string-equality.

rules.name: named_pattern_enables_design_introspection
rules.head: Jabberwock's introspection is asked about its runtime
rules.body: with this Mt installed, the answer is no longer 'I use a hash table somewhere' — it's 'I use typed_graph_arena_layout_pattern, which composes arenas + interners + edge tuples + Γ triple-index. Walk this Mt for the rationale per component.' The substrate gains introspectable knowledge of its own design.
